claims.text: Adding a low level of silicon to ZrB2 powder will enable densification at approximately 1600–1700 °C.
Silicon addition will promote formation of an intergranular amorphous SiO2 layer.
The intergranular silica phase will improve high-temperature oxidation resistance.
The intergranular silica phase will improve durability against liquid plating-metal corrosion.
Silicon-modified ZrB2 can retain mechanical strength and structural integrity despite lower-temperature processing.
Conventional single-phase ZrB2 typically requires sintering above 2300 °C to achieve full densification.
Conventional single-phase ZrB2 typically requires sintering above 2300 °C to achieve optimal mechanical properties.
Silicon acts as a sintering aid in ZrB2 by enhancing mass transport.
Silicon in the material preferentially oxidizes during service to form silica.
The resulting silica barrier limits oxygen ingress into the ZrB2 matrix.
The resulting silica barrier limits penetration by liquid plating metal.
Limiting oxygen and liquid-metal penetration preserves the integrity of the ZrB2 matrix.
Lower-temperature Si-doped ZrB2 will have mechanical strength comparable to or better than conventionally sintered and lower-temperature undoped ZrB2.
Lower-temperature Si-doped ZrB2 will have markedly better high-temperature oxidation resistance than conventionally sintered and lower-temperature undoped ZrB2.
Lower-temperature Si-doped ZrB2 will have markedly better liquid-metal corrosion durability than conventionally sintered and lower-temperature undoped ZrB2.
The proposed benefits can persist at service temperatures up to around 2000 °C when exposure remains within the stability limits of silica.
Performance may diminish when service conditions exceed the stability limits of the silica phase.
